title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: we observed long-tail latency regressions and request starvation during peak traffic for mixed-priority workloads using the continuous batcher. This PR tunes the scheduler queueing policy, improves fairness across priority classes, and introduces starvation timeouts/metrics so low-priority requests cannot be indefinitely deferred. Summary of changes: 1) introduce a weighted fair-queueing (WFQ)-inspired admission layer to the continuous batcher scheduler that enforces per-priority tokens and refill rates; 2) add an exponential backoff timeout counter and a hard starvation cutoff that forces a small dedicated slot allocation when a request exceeds the configured starvation threshold; 3) introduce a dynamic queue-length-based migrate-to-new-batch heuristic to avoid head-of-line blocking from very long sequences; 4) surface new metrics (queue.wait_time_p50/p95/p99, starvation.count, forced_slot_alloc.count, wfq.demoted_requests) and expose config knobs via runtime flags for Dedicated/Private customers; 5) add comprehensive unit and integration tests and a simulation harness used for performance validation. Benchmarks: on internal perf lab (A100-hosted cluster) using mixed-small (short chat) + mixed-large (long generation) traffic, p99 latency for short requests decreased by ~18% at 95th percentile peak load and starvation events dropped from 4.2/min to 0.1/min; end-to-end throughput improved by ~6% due to reduced unnecessary batching waits. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2, enable in canary pool for 48 hours, validate metrics, then rollout to remaining pools with gradual ramp. Related: Linear items ENG-8421, ENG-8473. Breaking change: no. Release notes: improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention; configurable starvation_timeouts and metrics for operational visibility.

review_comments: Miguel Torres (review): Nice approach. Two requests: add an explicit conserved_capacity metric so we can track the forced-slot allocations, and document the expected WFQ weights for our standard priority tiers.
Ava Chen (author reply): Added forced_slot_alloc.count and documented default weights in config.py. Also added a short blurb in docs/observability.
Priya Nair (review): Can we add a safety valve to disable wfq_admission under extreme OOM conditions? I saw one simulation where reserve tokens caused slightly higher memory in corner cases.
Ava Chen (author reply): Implemented a fallback path that disables wfq admission and reverts to simple FIFO when free_memory_pct < 6%. Added unit test for fallback.
Jonah Rivera (approval): Verified perf numbers in canary; approving to merge once CI green.
discussion_summary: Reviewers requested additional metrics and a memory-safety fallback; author implemented both. Performance validated in perf harness and on canary. No functional API changes; all behavior gated behind runtime flag.

changelog_entry: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and introduced starvation prevention/timeouts. Exposed runtime flags and new metrics for operability.
release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention. New metrics: queue.wait_time_p50/p95/p99, starvation.count, forced_slot_alloc.count. Default behavior is feature-flagged behind continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout. Enable in canary pool for 48 hours, monitor queue.wait_time and starvation.count; then ramp to 25%/50%/100% across remaining pools with one-hour gaps.
testing: Unit tests covering WFQ refill and starvation; integration test exercising mixed priority workloads; perf simulation scripts included and results attached in perf/simulations/README.md.
notes: This change targets production pain points during mixed workload peaks. Ops should ensure continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 is toggled off if unusual memory pressure is observed.
examples: alert suggestion: starvation_count > 5/min for 3m -> page SRE
